 :J U D G M E N T:

This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 06.02.2022.
2.

The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 06.02.2022 at about 4.45 p.m. the petitioner was riding his Scooter bearing Reg.
No. KA-02-HU-7512, from Cubbon Road, on BRV Junction, near CTO Circle, Cubbon Park Metro, Bangalore, at that time another Scooter bearing No. KA- 03-KC-8496 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Hemavathi Hospital, Tumkur, wherein he was treated conservatively.
He was discharged with an advise to take follow-up treatment.

The petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, medicine,
conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges and Rs.15,000/- towards repair of his Scooter.

The petitioner was aged about 45 years and he was Home Guard, BEML Soudha +
Home Guard office at Ulsoor and earning a sum of Rs.31,834/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries, he has lost his earnings.
In future he cannot do any avocation due to disability.
The 1 st respondent being the R.C. owner of above said Scooter and the 2nd respondent being its insurer, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, this petition.
3. After service of notice, 2nd respondent-Insurance company appeared through it's counsel and filed written statement.

In so far as 1st respondent- R.C. owner of offending vehicle is concerned,
she remained absent and she has been placed Ex-parte.

4. The written statement averments of the 2nd respondent are hereunder:
There is no compliance of Sec.158(6) & Sec.134(c) of M.V.Act.

The issuance of insurance policy with respect to Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-8496 is admitted,
however, the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of policy.

This Basavaraju vs Anusha Nayak on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197441749/
2 respondent submits that the alleged accident took place on 06.02.2022, however the complaint was lodged on 12.02.2022 after lapse of 6 days from the date of alleged accident.

Further contended that the rider of the Scooter bearing No.
KA-03-KC-8496 was not holding a valid and effective driving license as on the date of the alleged accident.
Injuries sustained by the petitioner, age, avocation and income of the petitioner, amount spent by the petitioner and permanent disability sustained by him is also denied.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following:
:ISSUES:
1 . Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries on 06.02.2022 on account of negligence of rider of Scooter bearing Registration No.KA-03-KC-8496 as stated in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the reliefs sought for?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16, Ex.P24 and Ex.P25.
Further, he examined 3 witnesses as P.W.2 to P.W.4 and marked Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.23.
P.W.1 to P.W.4 were cross- examined from the side of respondent No.2.

Respondent No.2 examined PSI as RW.1 and marked document as Ex.R1 and also examined its Assistant Legal Manager as R.W.2 and marked Ex.R.2.
7.
Heard the arguments from both side.
8. Perused the records placed before the Tribunal.

The findings of this Tribunal to the above referred Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 :- In the Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :- As per the final order, for the following:

:REASONS:
9.
ISSUE No.1:-
In order to prove this issue, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7.

Accordingly,
Ex.P.1 is the true copy of FIR pertaining to Cr.No.4/2022.
Ex.P.2 is the true copy of Complaint.

Basavaraju vs Anusha Nayak on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197441749/
3
Ex.P3 is the true copy of charge sheet.
Ex.P.4 is the true copy of spot mahazar.
Ex.P.5 is the true copy of spot sketch.
Ex.P.6 is the true copy of M.V.A. Report.
Ex.P.7 is the true copy of wound certificate.

In addition to that, petitioner has examined the eye witness as P.W.4.
10.
According to the petitioner, he has sustained injuries in the road accident.
According to the 2 nd respondent- Insurance company, the offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the other two motor vehicles were involved in the accident.
The petitioner has filed the petition after thought by twisting the facts to get compensation.

11. In order to substantiate the contentions of written statement, 2nd respondent has examined PSI,
Control Room as RW-1 and marked document at Ex.R.1 i.e., charge sheet and Case dairy and examined its Assistant Legal Manager namely Vallabha Bai Patil as R.W.2.
R.W.2 has filed the affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
In support of his evidence, R.W.2 has marked Ex.R.2.
Ex.R.2 is the insurance policy.

12. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".
13. In the instant case, the petitioner has produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.2, complaint was lodged before Cabbon Park Traffic Police Station on 12.02.2022.
Thereafter, as per Ex.P.1, FIR was lodged against the rider of Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-8496.

Further, on careful perusal of Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.3, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.3 after completing investigation.
A careful perusal of Ex.P.3, it clearly goes to show that, the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Further, on perusal of Ex.P.3 i.e., final report, it reveals that, the rider of offending vehicle i.e., Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-8496 arrayed as accused.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs.
Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
14.

entities.text: High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The evidence of P.W.4 also inspires the confidence of this Tribunal and the above referred decisions are aptly applicable to the case on hand.

At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveal that, when the petitioner was riding his Scooter, the another Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-8496 came in a rash or negligent manner with high and dashed to the petitioner.

The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that the rider of Scooter Basavaraju vs Anusha Nayak on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197441749/
4 bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-8496 has caused the accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.2:- This issue is with respect to entitlement of relief.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, accident was occurred due to rash or negligent riding of the Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-8496 by its rider.
The 2nd respondent is the insurer and the 1 st respondent is the R.C. owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
Before going to discuss other aspects, it is appropriate to discuss the age and income of the petitioner.
According to the petitioner, he was aged 45 years as on the date of accident.
In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.9, the notarized copy of his Aadhaar Card.
On perusal of this document it appears to this Tribunal that, the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 05.12.1977.
The accident was occurred on 06.02.2022.
Hence, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 45 years.
Accordingly the age of the petitioner is considered as 45 years.
17. Income:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he was working as Home Guard, he was earning Rs.31,834/- per month.
Per-contra, the 2 nd respondent has denied the income of petitioner.
To substantiate the income of petitioner, he has produced bank statements, which have marked as Ex.P.24 and Ex.P.25.
As per Ex.P.25, during the month of November-2021, Rs.13,730/-
was credited to the account of petitioner.
Further as per Ex.P.24, on 06.01.2022, Rs.18,511/- was credited to the account of petitioner.
Further, on 07.02.2022, Rs.18,531/- has been credited to the account of petitioner.
Further, as per Ex.P.11, gross salary has been shown as Rs.21,465/- and Rs.200/- has been deducted towards profession tax.
After deducting the professional tax, the net salary become Rs.21,265/-.
Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.21,265/- per month.

18. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has averred that, he has sustained complete tear of anterior cruciate ligament of right knee, complete tear of medial collateral ligament at its femoral attachment and chip fracture of posterior aspect of lateral tibial plateau right.
He has produced wound certificate, which is marked as Ex.P7.
On perusal of Ex.P.7-Wound certificate it reveals that, the petitioner has sustained injuries.

It is relevant to mention that, respondent No.2 has disputed the injuries caused to P.W.1.
19.
The petitioner has examined one witness namely G.V.Madhu, Manager, Medical Record Department at Hemavathi Orthopedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkur P.W.2.

entities.text: Hemavathi Orthopedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: P.W.2 in his evidence stated that, the petitioner was taken treatment at Hemavathi hospital for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident.

He has produced authorization letter, MLC extract, Police Intimation,
Case sheet as per Ex.P.17 to Ex.P20.
20.

In order to prove the physical disability/injuries, the petitioner examined medical witness namely Dr.S. Ramachandra, Senior Consultant at General Hospital, Jayanagar, Bangalore as P.W.3.
Basavaraju vs Anusha Nayak on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197441749/
5

This witness has filed the affidavit in lieu of evidence and stated that the petitioner has sustained complete tear of anterior cruciate ligament of right knee, complete tear of medial collateral ligament at its femoral attachment and chip fracture of posterior aspect of lateral tibial plateau right .

Further deposed that, he was examined the petitioner on 17.11.2022 for the disability assessment and found that, the petitioner has complete ACL tear of right knee shows post reconstruction status with implants in situ and MCL tear shows repair with implants in situ.
Finally he has assessed the total physical disability of right lower limb as 32.32% and 16.66% to the whole body.
He was cross- examined from the side of respondent at length.
During the course of cross-examination, he has admitted that, he was not the treated doctor.
He also admitted that, the fractures are united and there is normal in hip movement.
He also admitted that, he has assessed only physical disability and not the functional disability.

P.W.3 has produced 2 documents, which have marked as Ex.P.21 and Ex.P.22.
21.
On perusal of the discharge summaries of petitioner and evidence of medical witness clearly reveals that, petitioner has sustained injury and suffered physical deformity.
Now the question before this Tribunal is whether such physical deformity affects his earnings or not?.
It is relevant to note that, petitioner has produced his bank statements, which have been marked as Ex.P.24 and Ex.P.25.
It is further relevant to note that, during the course of cross-examination of P.W.1, he has clearly deposed that, he has no impediment to produce further bank statement.
However, the petitioner has not furnished his bank statement subsequent to the month of April- 2022.

22. It is relevant to note that, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 suggested that, the petitioner has intentionally withhold the bank statement for the month of May-2022, the said suggestion was denied by P.W.1.
It is important to note that, the said suggestion played vital role to ascertain loss of future income of the petitioner.
If really the petitioner has not resume to his avocation, what was the impediment for him to produce his further bank statement from May-2022 till 2025.
In other words, it is not forthcoming from the side of petitioner why he has not produced his bank statement from May-2022 till 2025.

Therefore, it appears to this Tribunal that, subsequent to his accident also,
the petitioner has continued his work.
Further it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner has deliberately not produced his bank statements from May- 2022 to till 2025.
As such evidence of P.W.3 will not come to the aid of petitioner with respect to loss of future earnings.
Under such circumstances, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of Future Income due to disabiltiy.
23. Medical Expenses:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he has incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment chages etc.
In order to substantiate the incurring of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced medical bills of Hemavathi Hospital for Rs.1,56,567/- as Ex.P.12.
This Tribunal has carefully perused Ex.P.12, the medical bills.
There is no contrary evidence from the respondents to disbelive the medical bills.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,56,567/- towards medical expenses.

24. Pain and suffering:- According to the petitioner, immediately after the accident he went to Hemavathi Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkur on 07.02.2022, wherein his right leg has been operated and inserted spring to his right leg and he was discharged on 11.02.2022 with an advise to Basavaraju vs Anusha Nayak on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197441749/
6 take follow up treatment.

entities.text: Hemavathi Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the medical records produced by the petitioner, it appears to this Tribunal the petitioner has taken certain treatment.
Further, on perusal of Ex.P.7- Wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries and taken treatment.
25. Further, as per the evidence of doctor, it appears to this tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident.
There is no serious dispute with regard to inpatient for a period of 5 days.
As such, the petitioner suffered a lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal grants compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

26. Loss of income during the laidup period:-
According to petitioner the doctors have advised him to take follow-up treatment as such he visited the hospital on several occasions.
However, the petitioner has not produced documents to show that, how many days he has taken bed rest.
Naturally it shows that, he might have taken atleast one month rest because of the injuries.
He has averred that, he was working as a Security Guard and earning Rs.31,834/- per month.

This Tribunal has already assessed the income of petitioner as Rs.21,265/-
per month.
Hence, one month is to be considered as loss of income during laidup period.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.21,265/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
27. Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges:-
The petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient in the hospital for the period of 5 days.
P.W.1 has stated that, he visited the hospital after one month from the discharge and then once in 15 days for 2 months and thereafter once in month.
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the petitioner has not produced any documents in this regard.

Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- under the head of Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges.
28. Loss of future amenities and happiness:- The petitioner was aged about 45 years at the time of accident.
The disability and physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Therefore, he might have suffered pain, discomforts in life and loss of amenities.
By considering the age, nature of injuries, percentage of disabiltiy, Rs.10,000/- is awarded under this head.
29. Future medical expenses:-
The petitioner has stated that, he reqires approximately a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards removal of implants and towards future medical expenses.
P.W.3, the medical witness deposed that, the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant from right femur.
Hence, by considering the future treatment and evidence of P.W.3, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards future medical expenses.

30. Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

 happiness.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.2,42,832/-
31.
Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License:-
According to respondsent No.2, the rider of offending vehicle has no valid driving licence to drive the vehicle.
The charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that rider of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.
Therefore, it can be inferred that, the rider of the offending vehicle was holding valid D.L. to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Insurance Policy and liability:-
In the instant case, respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-8496.
Hence, the respondent No.2 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioner.

32. In view of the decision reported in MFA NO: 30131- 2019 dtd, 12.5.2020 and M.F.A.No.100090/2014 C/w M.F.A.No.25107/2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and Others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and Another, rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition.

entities.text:
Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and Others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is clarified that, future medical expenses does not carry any interest.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the Partly Affirmative.
33. ISSUE No.3:- In view of discussions made above, I proceed to pass the following.

:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the petition.
Basavaraju vs Anusha Nayak on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197441749/
8

Petitioner is awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.2,42,832/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Forty Two Thousand Eight Hundred and Thirty Two only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
However, it is clarified that, the compensation awarded under the head of future medical expenses does not carry any interest.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.

:APPORTIONMENT:
The scheme of investment is dispensed with as the compensation awarded is meager amount.

A careful perusal of Ex.P.3, it clearly goes to show that, the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Further, on perusal of Ex.P.3 i.e., final report, it reveals that, the rider of offending vehicle i.e., Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-8496 arrayed as accused.
The evidence of P.W.4 also inspires the confidence of this Tribunal and the above referred decisions are aptly applicable to the case on hand.
At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveal that, when the petitioner was riding his Scooter, the another Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-8496 came in a rash or negligent manner with high and dashed to the petitioner.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that the rider of Scooter Basavaraju vs Anusha Nayak on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197441749/
4 bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-8496 has caused the accident.
The 2nd respondent is the insurer and the 1 st respondent is the R.C. owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
Further it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner has deliberately not produced his bank statements from May- 2022 to till 2025.
As such evidence of P.W.3 will not come to the aid of petitioner with respect to loss of future earnings.
Under such circumstances, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of Future Income due to disabiltiy.
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he has incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment chages etc.
There is no contrary evidence from the respondents to disbelive the medical bills.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,56,567/- towards medical expenses.
Hence, one month is to be considered as loss of income during laidup period.
According to respondsent No.2, the rider of offending vehicle has no valid driving licence to drive the vehicle.
Therefore, it can be inferred that, the rider of the offending vehicle was holding valid D.L. to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
In the instant case, respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-8496.
